# firecrawl map

Discover URLs on a site. Use `--search` to find a specific page within a large site.

**Prerequisite:** `map` requires authentication (no keyless free tier); without credentials the CLI prompts an interactive login.

## Quick start

```bash
# Find a specific page on a large site
firecrawl map "<url>" --search "authentication" -o .firecrawl/filtered.txt

# Get all URLs
firecrawl map "<url>" --limit 500 --json -o .firecrawl/urls.json
```

Run `firecrawl map --help` for the full option list (sitemap handling, subdomains, etc.).

For "every page about X", `--search` ranks a subset: raise `--limit`, read the whole list and keep every matching URL (ignore translated copies), not just the top few.

**Done when:** the URL list is saved under `.firecrawl/` and you have selected the URLs to scrape or crawl next.

## Tips

- **Map + scrape is a common pattern**: use `map --search` to find the right URL, then `scrape` it.
- Example: `map https://docs.example.com --search "auth"` → found `/docs/api/authentication` → `scrape` that URL.

## See also

- [firecrawl-scrape](../firecrawl-scrape/SKILL.md) — scrape the URLs you discover
- [firecrawl-crawl](../firecrawl-crawl/SKILL.md) — bulk extract instead of map + scrape
- [firecrawl-download](../firecrawl-download/SKILL.md) — download entire site (uses map internally)
- [firecrawl-build-search](https://github.com/firecrawl/skills/tree/main/skills/build/firecrawl-build-search) — building URL discovery into an app instead of running it here

Vercel's docs now call this product **Global Config**. `/docs/edge-config` returns a 308 redirect, so the old URL still works. I found these URLs by mapping vercel.com/docs. I scraped only the main page and didn't read the others. Their descriptions come from their URL paths.

**Core docs** (`https://vercel.com/docs/global-config` and subpages)
- `/docs/global-config`: overview of what it is and how it works.
- `/docs/global-config/using-global-config`: how to create and use it.
- `/docs/global-config/global-config-sdk`: the SDK for reading values.
- `/docs/global-config/global-config-dashboard`: managing it in the dashboard.
- `/docs/global-config/vercel-api`: managing it through the API.
- `/docs/global-config/global-config-limits`: limits and quotas.
- `/docs/global-config/migration-guide`: migration guide.
- `/docs/global-config/global-config-integrations`: integrations index.
  - `/docs/global-config/global-config-integrations/launchdarkly-global-config`: LaunchDarkly.
  - `/docs/global-config/global-config-integrations/statsig-global-config`: Statsig.
  - `/docs/global-config/global-config-integrations/devcycle-global-config`: DevCycle.

**CLI**
- `/docs/cli/global-config`: the `vercel` CLI commands for it.

**REST API reference**, under `/docs/rest-api/global-config/…`
- `create-a-global-config`
- `get-global-config-schema`
- `update-global-config-schema`
- `get-global-config-backup`
- `get-global-config-token-meta-data`
- `delete-one-or-more-global-config-tokens`

**REST API SDK reference**, under `/docs/rest-api/sdk/global-config/…`
- `create-a-global-config`
- `get-global-config-items`
- `get-a-global-config-item`
- `get-global-config-schema`
- `delete-a-global-config-s-schema`
- `get-all-tokens-of-a-global-config`
- `delete-one-or-more-global-config-tokens`
- `restore-global-config-backup`

Two related SDK pages are `/docs/rest-api/sdk/edge-config/get-edge-config-token-meta-data` (the one page still under the old "edge-config" name) and `/docs/rest-api/sdk/marketplace/get-the-data-of-a-user-provided-global-config-1`.

**Vercel MCP tools** (these still use the old name), under `/docs/agent-resources/vercel-mcp/tools/global-config/…`
- `get_edge_configs`
- `create_edge_config`
- `create_edge_config_token`
- `get_edge_config_backups`

Appending `.md` to a docs URL, such as `/docs/global-config.md`, returns a markdown version of the page. The mapped results also included `/docs/functions/runtimes/edge`, which covers the Edge runtime for Functions. That is a different feature from Edge Config.
